title: Cbi vs Avinash Chander on 25 September, 2024
doc:
Cbi vs Avinash Chander on 25 September, 2024

  IN THE COURT OF MS. NEELOFER ABIDA PERVEEN:
SPECIAL JUDGE (PC ACT) (CBI) ROUSE AVENUE COURTS
              COMPLEX, NEW DELHI.


Crl.Rev. No.24/2020
Central Bureau of Investigation
Through Mr. Nishender Diwakar

Vs.

Avinash Chander
S/o Late Sh. Ram Lubhaya
R/o B 101, Himhit CGHS, Plot no.8,
Sec.22, Dwarka, New Delhi.


Date of institution: 06.03.2020
Date of Judgment: 25.09.2024


                         JUDGMENT

1. The present revision petition has been revived in pursuance to order dated 21.08.2023 passed by Hon'ble the High Court of Delhi in Crl. M.C. no. 1070/2021 setting aside order dated 05.12.2020 passed by my Ld. Predecessor in Crl. Rev. No. 24/2020. This matter was remitted to this Court by Hon'ble the High Court of Delhi with the direction to decide the application u/Sec. 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963, prior to passing an order on the Revision Petition on merits. The application of CBI u/Sec. 5 of Limitation Act, 1963 was allowed vide order dated 08.02.2024 passed by this Court, and consequently, in accordance, with the directions contained in order dated 21.08.2023 of H'ble the High Court of Delhi in Crl. M.C. No. 1070/2021, this Revision Petition Page No. 1 of 35 is being taken up for final disposal on merits.

2. It emerges that two Revision petitions i.e. Cr. No. 4/2020 preferred by accused and Crl. Rev. No. 24/2020 filed by CBI were decided vide common order dated 05.12.2020, while Crl. Rev.No. 4/2020 was dismissed, Crl. Rev. No. 24/2020 i.e. CBI's revision petition was accepted. It has been clarified that though the order impugned dated 05.12.2020 passed by my Ld. Predecessor was a common order passed in Cr.No.4/20 and 24/2020, however, the accused/ respondent had challanged the said common order before H'ble the High Court of Delhi in the present revision petition alone, i.e. in Cr. No. 24/2020. CBI has filed the present Revision Petition assailing order on charge dated 14.11.2019, passed by Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap, the then Ld. CMM, Rouse Avenue Court, New Delhi, in case RC-EOU-I 2006 E 0004/-DLI titled as CBI Vs. Ajit Singh & Others, to the extent that accused/respondent Avinash Chander (A-2) has been discharged of the offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 420 IPC & substantive offences u/Sec. 420 IPC.

3. A brief backdrop is necessary before progressing on merits to attain a better perspective, this being the second round. It emerges that the Ld. Trial Court vide order on charge dated 14.11.2019 passed in RC-EOU-I 2006 E0004, had discharged accused Ajit Singh (A-1) and accused Ashutosh Pant (A-5) of all offences, and had proceeded against accused Avinash Chander (A-2) and accused Ashwani Sharma (A-3) for the commission of offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 468/471 IPC, and the substantive offences u/Sec. 468/471 IPC, and against accused Naveen Page No. 2 of 35 Kaushik (A-4), for commission of offence u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 468 IPC and the substantive offence thereof, while discharging all the accused, there being 5 arraigned under the chargesheet submitted in Court in RC-EOU-I 2006 E0004, including the accused/ respondent Avinash Chander, u/Sec. 120-B IPC r/w Sec. 420 IPC and the substantive offence u/Sec. 420 IPC on the ground that membership in a Society is not a property relying upon the law laid down by H'ble the High Court of Delhi in A. P. Narang Vs. CBI (Cr. R.P. No. 397/2010, DOD 17.01.2011).

4. Six Revision petitions arose out of this Order on Charge dated 14.11.2019. CBI itself had instituted 5 separate Revision petitions (CR No.24/2020, 25/2020, 26/2020, 27/2020 & 28/2020) challenging the discharge of each one of the accused for the various offences. Accused /respondent, Avinash Chander had filed a separate Revision Petition (CR No. 4/20) questioning the charges ordered to be framed qua him u/Sec.120-B r/w Sec. 468, 471 IPC, and the substantive offences therein. As noted earlier, Revision petition no. 4/2020 lodged by Avinash Chander, the accused/respondent, was disposed of alongwith the present Revision petition of CBI (CR no. 24/2020), vide a common order dated 05.12.2020, while separate orders though of the same date, were passed in the remaining four petitions of CBI. All the 5 Revision petitions preferred by CBI against Order on Charge dated 14.11.2019 were allowed vide separate orders of even date ie 05.12.2020.

5. Accused Ajit Singh had challenged order dated 05.12.2020 passed in the Revision petition instituted by CBI i.e. CR No. Page No. 3 of 35 28/2020 challenging his discharge vide Crl. M.C. No. 2470/2020, which was decided on 23.12.2020, accused Avinash Chander had presented another petition i.e. Crl. M.C. No. 1070/2021 u/Sec. 482 Cr.PC for setting aside the order dated 05.12.2020 vide which Revision Petition of CBI i.e. CR No. 24/20 calling into question his discharge u/Sec. 120 B r/w Sec. 420 IPC, and the substantive offence of 420 IPC. H'ble the High Court of Delhi disposed of the said petition of the accused/respondent vide order dated 21.08.2023, accepting the contention of the accused/ respondent herein, who was the petitioner before the H'ble High Court, that the impugned order was passed without deciding the application of CBI seeking condonation of delay.

6. The submissions made before H'ble the High Court in the said petition and the directions passed in the light thereof are reproduced hereunder:-

"2. Ld. Counsel for the petitioner, before going into the merits of the matter, submits that the limitation to file the revision petition against the order dated 14.11.2019 expired on 12.02.2020. The revision petition had been belatedly filed by the respondent/ CBI alongwith an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 seeking condonation of delay in filing the said petition. He further submits that the impugned order dated 05.12.2020 was passed by the Ld. Special Judge without adjudicating the said application of the respondent/ CBI seeking condonation of delay.
.............
4. The perusal of the impugned order dated 05.12.2020 shows that the learned Special Judge (PC Act) (CBI), Rouse Avenue District Court, New Delhi has proceeded to hear and decide the revision petition filed by the respondent/ CBI without dealing and adjudicating upon the application filed by CBI for condonation of delay in filing the revision petition. .............
6. Accordingly, the impugned order dated 05.12.2020 passed by the learned Special Judge (PC Act) (CBI), Rouse Avenue District Court, New Delhi is set aside and the matter is Page No. 4 of 35 remitted to the learned Special Judge, (PC Act) (CBI), Rouse Avenue Courts, New Delhi for deciding the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 filed by the respondent/ CBI prior to passing an order on revision petition on merits."

7. Adverting now to the contentions and counter submissions made before this Court in the present petition on merits, Ld. PP for CBI submitted that the present case was registered in pursuance to the directions of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi dated 03.10.2005 in Civil Writ Petition no.10066/2004, u/Sec. 120B, r/w 420, 468, 471 IPC and 13(2) r/w 13(1)(d) of PC Act 1988 and the substantive offences thereof against accused Ajit Singh, Avinash Chander, Smt. Sudha Gupta, Vishal Aggarwal, Ashwani Sharma, Dilip Bhattacharya, Maheswar Dutt Sharma and other unknown persons in respect of the Society, Vishrantika CGHS Ltd. That the said Society was registered with the office of RCS, New Delhi on 07.01.1984 with 65 promoter members, that accused/respondent Avinash Chander (A-2), the then Secretary of the Society had forwarded a revised list of 90 members of the Society to the RCS office alongwith his affidavit dated 27.02.1998 mentioning therein that payments had been made to the members who had resigned.

(i) That the documents submitted in the RCS office in respect of 90 members by accused/respondent contained four forged affidavits in the names of Smt. Nirmal Maini ( M no.92), Sh.Subhash Kumar Diwan (M no.89), Sh. Vinod Sharma (M No.123) and Sh. Satish Sharma (M-122), and two forged enrollment applications of Vinod Sharma and Satish Sharma.

This list of 90 members was verified by Sh. Dalip Bhattacharya Page No. 5 of 35 and forwarded by Sh. Maheshwar Dutt Sharma to Assistant Registrar (Policy) on 25.3.1998, with the approval of the RCS. On 03.06.1998, the Society was allotted land by DDA at Dwarka. That Ajit Singh (A-1), the then Secretary of the Society, later had sought reduction of members in the freeze list from 90 to 80, which was acceded to, and this list of 70 members bearing the signatures of Ajit Singh, Secretary, Vikas Aggarwal, President, Smt. Sudha Gupta, Vice President was forwarded by RCS on 02.04.2004 to DDA for allotment of flats. That the Society had constructed 80 flats and allotted 72 flats to its members on 13.06.2004.

(ii) That after allotment of land to the Society by DDA on 03.06.1998, fake resignations of Smt. Nirmal Maini (M No 92), Sh. Subhash Kumar Diwan (M No 89), Sh. Vinod Sharma (M No

123) and Sh. Satish Sharma (M No 122), Smt. Shashi Kumar Diwan (M No 86) and Smt. Inderjit Kaur (M No 167) were forwarded to RCS office by accused Ajit Singh and after construction of flats, the names of the said members were excluded from the final list of members to whom flats were allotted. That accused Ajit Singh engaged accused Ashwani Sharma and Naveen Kaushik for writing fake proceedings of the Society and also completing the other documentation. That accused Ashutosh Pant filled in some particulars like membership number, name of members, date, etc. in the forged resignation letters, vouchers and other documents which were submitted to the RCS office for allotment of land and flats.

(iii) That there is sufficient material produced on the record to Page No. 6 of 35 show that accused Ajit Singh (A-1), Avinash Chander (A-2) the then Secretary Vishrantika Society, Ashwani Sharma (A-3), Naveen Kaushik (A-4) and Ashutosh Pant (A-5) entered into a criminal conspiracy during the year 1998 to 2004 and in furtherance of said criminal conspiracy resignations of some genuine members were forged and accepted and in place new members of their own choice were enrolled for allotment of land to the Society from DDA at concessional rate, and allotment of flats to the said members. That CBI has challenged the order on charge only to the extent that the accused/respondent has been discharged of the offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 420 IPC, and S.420 IPC, that the accused/respondent otherwise is up for trial for commission of offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 468,471IPC and the substantive offences u/Sec. 468 and 471 IPC.

(iv) That the Ld. Trial Court while discharging the accused/ respondent of the offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 420 IPC, and S.420 IPC, failed to appreciate that accused/ respondent Avinash Chander (A-2) submitted a fabricated revised list of 90 members including the names of persons who never became members of the Society by showing resignation of some members and accepting enrollment of some others, alongwith his affidavit dated 27.02.1998 in the office of RCS mentioning therein that payments had been made to the members who had resigned and if there was any complaint regarding their genuineness he personally and on behalf of the Society undertakes entire liability in that behalf. That accused/respondent had also submitted along with the said list, respective forged and fabricated documents of Page No. 7 of 35 such fictitious members, thereby the RCS officials were misrepresented and deceived and as a result of which the aforesaid fabricated revised list of 90 members was got approved fraudulently by the accused /respondent Avinash Chander (A-2) in conspiracy with other co-accused persons on the basis of false and fabricated documents, on 19.03.1998, which revised list of 90 members, also known as the freeze list, was further submitted by RCS officials to DDA for allotment of land.

(v) That accused/respondent Avinash Chander (A-2), as Secretary of the Society prior to the preparation of aforesaid fabricated revised list of 90 members, had fraudulently accepted the enrollments of certain members in the proceedings dated 10.09.1996 of the Managing Committee of the Society. He had enrolled accused Ajit Singh as a member of the Society on 09.05.1998 and thereafter in pursuance of fake minutes election proceedings dated 10.07.1998, he was shown to have been elected as the executive committee member of the Society in violation of DCS Rules, within two months, which all facts and circumstances are sufficient to infer the factum of conspiracy on the part of accused/respondent Avinash Chander (A-2).

(vi) That the Ld. Trial Court has fallen in error in not appreciating that Ajit Singh also got envolved Vishal Aggarwal, Smt. Sudha Gupta & Sh. Trilochan Singh as members of the Society on 09.05.1998 and 10.06.1998, who were falsely shown to have been elected as President and Executive Committee Members of the Society in proceedings dated 10.07.1998. It is only after such alleged election that possession of the allotted Page No. 8 of 35 land in the name of Society was taken over by Ajit Singh on 01.09.2000 from the DDA.

(vii) That if DDA had been apprised that the management committee had not been elected in the alleged election, DDA would not have handed over the possession of the allotted land to Ajit Singh on behalf of Society/ or its alleged management committee. That it is not the requirement of law that both wrongful loss and wrongful gain should occur simultaneously for the offence of cheating to be completed, and it is sufficient if either wrongful gain or wrongful loss is shown to have occurred to attract the definition of dishonest intention. That in the present case forgery was done with malafide intention to deceive RCS and DDA for inclusion and deletion of certain members illegally on the basis of forged documents from the already prepared freeze list and subsequent thereto to deceive the DDA to make allotment of the land as well as flat on the basis of such altered/modified list. That the judgement cited in the impugned order has no bearing in the facts of the case, and is totally distinguishable on facts.

8. Ld. Counsel for the Respondent on the other hand submitted that the Respondent/accused has been wrongly arraigned as an accused in the chargesheet submitted in FIR no. RC EOU-I 2006 E-0004 by CBI on the basis of false, frivolous and baseless allegations. That the fact of the matter is that though the respondent was the Secretary of the Society in the name of Vishrantika CGHS Ltd. which was registered with the office of RCS on 07-01-1984, he had resigned from the membership of the Page No. 9 of 35 Society as well as from the Hony. post of Secretary of the Society in December, 1997. Even the amount deposited by the respondent herein towards his share money, was refunded to the respondent herein vide cheque bearing no.893521 dated 01-01-1998, for a sum of Rs.15,000/- and another cheque bearing no.893522 dated 15-01-1998 for a sum of Rs.20,000/-. That the said cheques were received late by the respondent due to non availability of the signatories and the same were deposited in the month of March, 1998 and cleared in the account of respondent herein.

(i) That the respondent was left with no concern with the above said Society thereafter nor with any interest in the land to be allotted to the Society for the reason that after resigning from the membership of the Society, the respondent herein could not have been allotted any flat, nor indeed was he allotted one, as such he has not obtained any benefit from the commission of the acts and omissions alleged against him. That only for the reason that there was no person in the Society to further process and complete the formalities and to correspond with the RCS Office, that the other office bearers of the Society had requested the respondent to continue at the post of Secretary for the time being till new Secretary is appointed, so that the allotment of land does not get hampered thereby. It was only with the intention to cooperate and under good faith that the respondent had continued working with the Society even after resignation.

(ii) That it is pertinent that land was not allotted during the time period of the respondent, as the same came to be allotted to the Society by the DDA on 03-06-1998 i.e. much after the Page No. 10 of 35 resignation of the respondent. That being the Secretary of the Society, as per Rule 44 of DCS Rules, the respondent being custodian of the records was under an obligation to keep all the records of the Society in his custody. That whatever application forms alongwith affidavits resignations and other documents were received by the respondent, as Secretary being custodian he was duty bound to accept the same. That the receipts with respect to the amount received were issued by the respondent as a part of duties of the Secretary and the same are duly accounted for. Even the amount refunded to the members who have resigned has also been duly accounted for and the same has also been verified by the RCS office. That the membership of the incoming members and resignations of the outgoing members are approved by the management committee. As the Secretary, the records pertaining to such proceedings, including the application forms of the members and their resignation letters were submitted by the respondent herein, in his capacity of Secretary, being custodian thereof, to the RCS Office.

(iii) That the respondent has played no role in the allotment of land or flats to the individual members or in the list of members that finally got allotted the flats. That the Ld. Trial Court has rightly held that there is no meeting of minds and no offence of cheating made out against the respondent. That when there is no cheating and no meeting of minds, in the absence of any material to show fraudulent and dishonest intention on the part of the respondent, he ought to be discharged of all offences in the present case, for it is not even the case of the revisionist CBI that Page No. 11 of 35 the respondent had forged any document, or had any knowledge that the documents were forged prior to submitting the same to the RCS Office, he is not alleged to be the author of the alleged documents by CBI. That even as per the forensic expert opinion, the alleged forged signatures on the alleged forged documents are not attributed to the respondent herein.

(iv) That no person has complained against the respondent herein that the respondent herein has forged his/ her signatures, or that it is the respondent herein, who has fraudulently made him/her, the member of the Society or has fraudulently got him/her resigned from the membership of the Society, or because of which the said persons has suffered any loss. That even the alleged signatures of Panna Lal, on the alleged resignation letter, has not been attributed to the respondent by the Forensic Expert. Moreover, the said Panna Lal has also not filed any complaint against the respondent herein that it is the respondent herein who has forged the said resignation letter or his signatures, or that he has suffered any loss because of the alleged forgery. Further mere denial of his signatures by the said Panna Lal without there being any other circumstantial evidence, cannot come within the purview of forgery or cheating, for that matter.

(v) That as most of the executives in the Society were working people and could not spare much time to complete the daily work of the Society, therefore, the services of one L.P. Sharma were hired to work as an accountant and for writing the proceedings, who had also been working for the other societies including one Society in the name of Pragatisheel CGHS Ltd.. One of the Page No. 12 of 35 members, namely Satish Sharma was also the member of the Society Pragtisheel CGHS Ltd., and as such the said L.P. Sharma was known to said Satish Sharma and his family members. That it is the said L.P. Sharma who had brought about 14 applications alongwith affidavit for enrollment as member of the Society, including that of the said Satish Sharma and his family members i.e., Vinod Sharma, Pawan Sharma and Narender Kumar. That it is in the statement of said L. P. Sharma, that the application forms were filled by him.

(vi) That the respondent, in the capacity of Secretary, had accepted these said application forms and affidavits brought by the said L. P. Sharma, duly supported with such documents like the Ration cards, etc., therefore, the respondent had no occasion to doubt the same. That even their respective ration cards have been duly admitted by the said concerned persons in their statements, it was then incumbent upon them to explain that how the copy of ration card had come in the record of the Society, if the application forms were not submitted by them, which aspect the CBI has not even examined. That the respondent had never written any proceedings of the Managing Committee, therefore there is no question of recording of fake proceedings by the respondent herein. That CBI has not even bothered to specify as to what fake proceedings were recorded and what and to whom, any loss has been caused from the said proceedings. That all the proceedings recorded during the tenure of the respondent are genuine.

(vii) That as per forensic expert opinion relied upon by CBI, Page No. 13 of 35 even the signatures of the respondent have been forged on certain proceedings as in the Annual General Meeting alleged to have been held on 10.07.1998 his signatures are shown marked as Q- 12, but these have not been attributed to the respondent herein by the Forensic expert, for the simple reason that the same were not signed by the respondent herein, as the respondent herein had already resigned, even in these proceedings respondent has been described as outgoing secretary, which demonstrates that the respondent had no connection with the affairs of the Society upon his resignation.

(viii) That no list of members and documents, were submitted by the respondent alongwith the affidavit dated 27.02.1998, no such fact has even been mentioned in the said affidavit. That the case of CBI is not clear as to which list was allegedly forwarded alongwith this affidavit, for, at one time, CBI alleges that the respondent has submitted first list of 90 members alongwith the affidavit dated 27.02.1998, and at the same time, CBI alleges that the respondent has submitted revised list of 90 members alongwith the affidavit dated 27.02.1998. Infact the affidavit dated 27.02.1998 was submitted by the respondent, as the same was required by the RCS offices, as a process of completing the formalities as per the format of the RCS offices, and the facts mentioned in the said affidavit are true and correct and on the basis of the record maintained by the Society, and duly verified by the RCS office.

(ix) That Ajit Singh had taken over the charge of the Society, w.e.f., 03.04.1998, even much before he became the member of Page No. 14 of 35 the Society on 09.05.1998, which is reflected from the notices issued by him as Secretary (at pages 503/с, 471/c and 453/c,), the respondent had no role even in the functioning of the Society, thereafter. That the proceedings dated 09.05.1998, 10.04.1998, 27.06.1998, were recorded by Ajit Singh, and as per the own case of the prosecution, it is Ajit Singh who had engaged Sh. Ashwani Sharma and Naveen Kaushik for writing the fake proceedings. That when the respondent never had any concern and never came in contact with the accused no. 3 and accused no. 4, then how can such an allegation be sustained that the respondent had conspired with other accused persons.

(x) That even otherwise, the respondent was nowhere in picture when the land was allotted to the Society, even the list alleged to have been submitted by the respondent herein vide his affidavit dated 27.02.1998, was not at all considered for allotment of flats to the members and it was the list submitted by the accused no.1 Ajit Singh vide his affidavit dated 31.03.2004 that was considered by the RCS office for draw of lots and for allotment of flats. The alleged revised list of 90 members submitted by the respondent was superseded by the list submitted by Ajit Singh as Secretary of the Society on the basis whereof the flats got allotted to the respective members. The allotment of flats to those 72 members was approved by DDA and RCS office, the respondent was not even present when the land was handed over or the flats got allotted. That DDA has not suffered any loss for the reason that the DDA had received the amount for the land, it allotted to the Society. That the chargesheet has been wrongly Page No. 15 of 35 filed against the respondent without any involvement of the respondent in the alleged offences committed by the other accused persons, infact it is a case of complete discharge so far as the respondent is concerned, though it is not disputed that the accused has been proceeded against for commission of offences u/Sec. 120B r/w Sec. 468 and 471 IPC, and the substantive offences thereof.

9. I have heard the Ld. PP for CBI, the Ld. Counsel for the accused/respondent, perused the record and also gone through the judicial pronouncements relied upon.

10. One Preliminary enquiry was registered by CBI, on 14.11.2005 on the directions of Hon'ble the High Court of Delhi contained in its order dated 03.10.2005 passed in Civil Writ Petition no.10066/2004, against the unknown office bearers of six Cooperative Group Housing Societies and as a culmination of this preliminary enquiry various FIR's were got registered in respect of irregularities in the different Societies. FIR RC No.EOU-I/2006/E0004, is one such case in respect of Society, Vishrantika CGHS Ltd., registered on 5.6.2006, u/Sec. 120B, r/w 420, 468, 471 IPC and 13(2) r/w 13(1)(d) of PC Act 1988 and the substantive offences thereof, against Ajit Singh, Avinash Chander, Smt. Sudha Gupta, Vishal Agarwal, Ashwani Sharma, Dilip Bhattacharya, Maheswar Dutt Sharma and other unknown persons, which array includes its past and present office bearers and some public servants from the RCS office.

11. Chargesheet dated 26.4.2007 for commission of offences u/Sec. 120B r/w Sec.420,468,471IPC and substantive offences Page No. 16 of 35 thereof was filed before the Ld. ACMM Karkardooma against Ajit Singh, Avinash Chander, Ashwani Kumar Sharma, Naveen Kaushik @ Pinki and Ashutosh Pant, while Sudha Gupta, Vikas Aggarwal, Dilip Bhattacharya and Maheshwar Dutt Sharma were placed in column no.12 of the chargesheet. Cognizance of the offences was taken on 27.4.2007, and vide Order on Charge dated 14.11.2019, Ajit Singh was fully discharged of all the alleged offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 420, 468, 471, IPC and the substantive offences u/Sec. 420 IPC and 471 IPC.

12. Avinash Chander, the respondent herein was partly discharged only for the offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 420 IPC, and the substantive offence under Section 420 IPC, while charges were ordered to be framed against him u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 468, 471, IPC and for the substantive offence u/Sec. 468 IPC and 471, IPC. Ashwani Sharma was also partly discharged only for the offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 420, IPC, and the substantive offence under Section 420 IPC, while charges were ordered to be framed against him u/Sec. 120B r/w Sec. 468, 471 IPC and for the substantive offence u/Sec. 468 IPC and 471 IPC. Naveen Kaushik was ordered to be proceeded against for offences u/Sec. 120B r/w Sec. 468 IPC, and the substantive offence u/Sec. 468 IPC, and was similarly discharged of the offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 420 IPC, and the substantive offence under Section 420 IPC, while Ashutosh Pant was also fully discharged of all the offences alleged against him, u/Sec. 120B r/w Sec. 420, 468, 471 IPC.

13. The challenge in the present revision petition to the Page No. 17 of 35 impugned Order on Charge dated 14.11.2019 is limited to the extent that accused/respondent Avinash Chander has been discharged of the offences u/Sec. u/Sec. 120B r/w Sec. 420, IPC, and the substantive offence under Section 420, IPC. It emerges that Vishrantika CGHS Ltd. was registered with the office of Registrar Cooperative Societies, New Delhi on 07.01.1984 vide Registration No.1279 (GH) with 65 promoter members. At the time of its registration, Sh. Mukhtiar Singh, accused Avinash Chander and Sh. Pawan Sahni were its office bearers being President, Secretary and Treasurer of the Society, respectively.

14. The case of the prosecution, as espoused under the chargesheet, is that after the Registration of the Society, twenty five more members were enrolled in the Society on 19.05.1985, accused Avinash Chander as Secretary furnished a list of 90 members to the office of RCS for approval and for forwarding the list to DDA vide his letter dated 30.07.1985. Accused Avinash Chander vide his letter dated 20.06.1986 had also filed an affidavit dated 26.06.1986 in the office of RCS certifying that none of the members had resigned after Registration of the Society while disclosing the details of the freshly enrolled twenty five new members in his affidavit. This list could not be approved by the RCS office, because the office bearers of the Society failed to produce the original records for verification despite multiple reminders from RCS office in this regard. Even a show cause notice u/Sec. 63(2)(b) of DCS Act, dated 08.07.91 was issued against the Society for its winding up and accused Avinash Chander submitted reply thereto on 15.07.1991 with an Page No. 18 of 35 undertaking that the Society would be taking all necessary steps but no one from the Society appeared in the RCS office for verification of the records.

15. It is alleged that thereafter accused Avinash Chander had submitted a revised list of 90 members alongwith his affidavit dated 27.02.1998 in the RCS office. This list included names of 29 members enrolled subsequent to the earlier list of 90 members that had been forwarded on 20.06.1986, separate lists, of the 29 members from the earlier list shown as resigned, of the 5 members who were enrolled and had resigned subsequent to 20.06.1986, were also furnished alongside. He had declared in the affidavit submitted alongwith, that payments had been made to the members who had resigned and if there arose any dispute regarding their genuineness he personally and on behalf of the Society undertakes entire liability in that behalf.

16. The relevant solemn affirmation is extracted below:

"2. That as per our records, also produced in the office of the R.C.S. for verification of enrollment and resignations, All refunds to the resigned Members were paid by cheques and which were also debited from the Society's Account.
3. That In any case, I certify that these payments have been made to the genuine resign Members. Still, if there is any complaint out of these members regarding the genuineness of their resignations, I personally and on behalf of the Society undertake entire liability in this behalf."

17. This revised list of 90 members bears the endorsement of the Managing Committee, certifying to the effect that the list of members before submission has been considered by the Managing Committee and the President of the Society and its Secretary have been authorised by the Managing Committee to Page No. 19 of 35 submit the list in the office of the Registrar Cooperative Societies. It has further been affirmed that all the members have been enrolled in accordance with the provisions of the Delhi Cooperative Societies Act, 1972 and Delhi Cooperative Societies Rules, 1973, made thereunder and the registered Bye-laws, and that the information given in the list is as per the records of the Society and nothing has been concealed/omitted/ misrepresented therein.

18. The revised list was submitted for the purposes of verification of membership of the Society by the RCS office, for the approval of the RCS and for forwarding the list of members of the Society to DDA for allocation of land, its each page is signed by the accused/respondent. This list was approved by the then RCS, Sh. Gopal Dixit on 19.03.1998, and was forwarded to the Asstt. Registrar (Policy) for further transmission to DDA under the signatures of the then Asstt. Registrar (SW), Sh. M.D. Sharma. Investigation unearthed that included in this list were five such Members, who had not even applied for membership of the Society, namely Sh. Amar Nath (M no.117), Sh. Narendra Kumar (M no.120), Sh. Pawan Sharma (M no.121), Sh. Satish Kumar (M no.122) and Sh. Vinod Kumar (M no.123). Their enrollment applications, affidavits etc. submitted by accused/respondent Avinash Chander (A-2) for verification and approval were forged. It also came to light that enrollments of these members were accepted in the proceedings dated 10.09.1996 of the Managing Committee of the Society by accused Avinash Chander as Secretary of the Society.

Page No. 20 of 35

19. There were four such members, namely Sh. Subhash Kumar Diwan (M No.89), Smt. Nirmal Maini (M.No.92), Smt. Shobha Chopra (M.No.101) and Smt. Prem Puri (M.No.105) included in this revised list of 90 members who though had become members of the Society but had never submitted any affidavit and their affidavits dated 26.02.1998 submitted to RCS office by accused/respondent Avinash Chander (A-2) for verification/approval have been forged. It is also found in investigation that accused/respondent as Secretary of the Society, accepted the forged resignations of five members namely Satish Kumar Sharma (M No.112), Kalu Ram (M No.21), Panna Lal (M No.32), J.K.Grover (M No.52), Smt. Niral Roda (M No.30), in the proceedings dated 09.05.98, 10.04.98, 27.06.98, 09.05.98 & 27.06.98, respectively, and that the signatures of Sh. Panna Lal (M No.32) on his resignation letter have been forged by accused/respondent, also that the resignation of Sh. P.K. Chadha (M.No.03) submitted by the accused/respondent to the RCS office for approval alongwith the aforesaid revised list of 90 members has been forged.

20. The accused/respondent has been proceeded against for commission of offences u/Sec. 120-B, r/w Sec. 468 and 471, IPC, and the substantive offences thereunder, and that aspect is not under challenge before this Court now in the present revision. It has been contended for the respondent that he has been wrongly proceeded against u/Sec. 468/471, IPC, there being no material to show that he has committed any forgery and that he being the custodian of the record as Secretary had merely submitted the Page No. 21 of 35 documents accepted by the Managing Committee of the Society, and provided by one L.P. Sharma working for the Society. It would not be appropriate for this Court seized of the present revision petition filed by CBI to reassess the material qua such allegations now, given that the respondent had opted not to challenge the dismissal of the revision petition that he had instituted (Crl. Rev.No.4/2020), questioning the correctness of the order framing these above charges against him, and had only assailed the common order passed in both CR.No.4/20 and Crl. Rev. No.24/20, to the extent that the revision petition filed by CBI (Crl. Rev. No.24/20) had been accepted, thereby limiting the challenge to that part of the order on charge only which pertains to his discharge u/s120-B r/w Sec. 420 IPC and the substantive offence of cheating u/Sec. 420 IPC. The subject matter of this revision petition is only the sustainability of that part of the order that relates to and results in his discharge for the offences u/Sec. 120-B r/w Sec. 420 IPC and the substantive offence of cheating u/Sec. 420 IPC

21. The Ld. Trial Court while proceeding against the accused/ respondent u/Sec. u/Sec. 120-B, r/w Sec. 468 and 471, and the substantive offences thereunder, has discharged him of the offence u/s120-B r/w Sec. 420 IPC and the substantive offence of cheating u/Sec. 420 IPC on the ground that there was no delivery of property involved which is one of the basic ingredients of the offence of cheating as membership in a Society cannot be said to be property or valuable security as held by H'ble the High Court of Delhi in A.P. Narang Vs. CBI (Crl. R. P. No. 397/2010, dated Page No. 22 of 35 17.01.2011. All cheating involves deception, but all deception is not cheating per se. Within the four corners of the definition embodied in Section 415 IPC, would lie such deception alone that fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property, or to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit to do if he were not so deceived, and then again not every act and omission intentionally caused by such deception would amount to cheating. Only such act or omission which causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind reputation or property would constitute the offence though even a dishonest concealment of facts is deception.

22. The punishment for cheating is provided u/Sec. 417 IPC, which may extend to one year with or without fine, the punishment for cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property invites higher degree of punishment extending upto 7 years with fine, prescribed u/Sec. 420 IPC. The essential ingredients of the offence are etched thereunder as follows:

"420. Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.-- Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine."

23. For proceeding against an accused for the commission of the offence of cheating u/Sec. 420 IPC, the dishonest inducement must be shown to have caused delivery of property to any person, or to have brought about the making, alteration, destruction of a valuable security even a part thereof, or of anything that is signed Page No. 23 of 35 and sealed and is capable of being converted into a valuable security. Simple offence of cheating punishable u/Sec. 417, IPC as such need not necessarily involve delivery of property/ valuable security as such, all that is required would be that the person deceived does something or omits to do something which such person would otherwise not have done or omitted to do but for such deception and which act/omission causes harm or damage to the said person.

24. Reverting to the case at hand, it is the case of the prosecution that the forged and fabricated record was submitted before the RCS office with the dishonest intention to induce the RCS office into forwarding the same to the Delhi Development Authority after verification of the documents and approval of the list at its end, for allotment of land to the Society and consequential allocation of flats to its individual members, upon determination of its freeze strength. So far as the role attributed to the accused/respondent as underscored in the earlier paragraphs is concerned, it is this revised list of 90 members submitted alongwith his affidavit dated 27.02.1998 by the accused/respondent as Secretary of the Society which became the freeze list on the basis whereof land got awarded to the Society, though the freeze strength was got modified by Ajit Singh later on in his capacity as Secretary and the flats to individual members came to be distributed on the basis of the subsequent list of 80 members submitted by Ajit Singh.

25. It is the fabricated documents supplied by accused/respondent alongwith this revised list of 90 members Page No. 24 of 35 and his affidavit dated 27.02.1998 that induced the RCS office into verifying and approving the list at its end before forwarding it to DDA for grant of land to the Society. To conclude then at this stage that there was no delivery of property involved is not in accordance with the record. The RCS office was deceived into doing a certain act on the strength of such forged and fabricated documents that is approving the revised list of 90 members and forwarding it to DDA for alottment of land to the Society, and DDA was deceived into processing the allotment of land to the Society on the strength of such verification and approval garnered on the basis of the forged and fabricated documents and revised list submitted by the accused/ respondent supported by his affidavit vouching for the correctness and genuineness thereof. As a matter of fact the land allocated by DDA to the Society is founded on this freeze list. Without the verification and approval of the list and record by RCS office, there would not have been allotment of any land to the Society by DDA.

26. As regards the angle of conspiracy, it is the prosecutions case, that when DDA was processing the proposal for allotment of land to various Societies in April-May, 1998, accused Ajit Singh in connivance with accused/respondent Avinash Chander (A-2) got himself enrolled as member of the Society on 09.05.1998. Thereafter in the fake election proceedings dated 10.07.1998 he was shown to have been elected as Executive Committee Member of the Society in violation of the DCS Rule No.59(k) which stipulates that no person shall be eligible for election as a member of the Managing Committee if he has not Page No. 25 of 35 completed minimum period of one year from the date of acquiring membership in the Society.

27. It is alleged that accused Ajit Singh started corresponding with DDA as Secretary of the Society, seeking extension of time for depositing the requisite amount towards the cost of land w.e.f. 02.07.1998 itself. There is then a volley of allegations qua Ajit Singh, numerous wrongdoings are attributed to him in cohorts with other accused, and I shall traverse such accusations and material, briefly though, only in this endeavour to explore the alleged illegal object or purpose behind this alleged conspiracy and no further. It is alleged that Ajit Singh got enrolled Sh. Vishal Aggarwal, Smt. Sudha Gupta and Sh. Trilochan Singh, as members of the Society on 09.05.1998 & 10.06.1998 and they were also falsely shown to have been elected President, and Executive Committee Members respectively of the Society in the proceeding dated 10.07.1998 of the Society. Accused Ajit Singh is alleged to have engaged accused Ashwani Sharma and Naveen Kaushik for writing fake proceedings of the Society including the fake proceedings of the general body meeting dated 25.06.2000 electing the Executive Committee Membes on the basis whereof he was handed over the possession of the land alotted to the Society by DDA in his capacity as Secretary of the Society, and also for completing the other documentation pertaining to inclusion and exclusion of desired and undesired members.

28. The Society was allotted land by DDA measuring 5000.21 Sq. Meters at plot No. 5A, Sector 3, Dwarka on 3.6.1998 and possession of the plot was taken by accused Ajit Singh on Page No. 26 of 35 01.09.2000 founded on such fake proceedings and record. Ajit Singht thereafter, got the freeze strength of the Society reduced from 90 to 80 from the DDA as well as RCS office and submitted a consolidated list of 80 members vide letter dated Feb. 2001, who had purportedly resigned after the freeze list which list includes nine members whose signatures on their resignations are alleged to have been forged. Thereafter a list of 121 resigned members was submitted in the RCS office vide letter dated 21.07.2003 of Ashwani Sharma in the capacity of office Secretary of the Society, which included the names of members in addition to the nine members whose resignation letters had been forged allegedly.

29. When the construction of the 80 flats of the Society was completed by the Society, for the allotment of the flats to the members, Ajit Singh filed an affidavit dt.31.03.2004 alongwith a list of 142 resigned members as well as 132 enrolled members subsequent to approval of freeze list bearing the names of the members whose resignation letters had been forged and after examination of the records of the Society the RCS and DDA approved the allotment of flats to only 72 members. Draw of flats was held on 13.06.2004 in the presence of the officials of the DDA, the RCS office and office bearers of the Society including Ajit Singh in their favour and accused Ajit Singh was also allotted flat no. A-32.

30. It is also transpired in investigation that flats of the Society were allotted only to those members who had made a payment for at least Rs.15 lacs whereas Sh. Trilochan Singh had made the Page No. 27 of 35 payment of Rs.1.10 lacs only and rest of the payment was arranged by Ajit Singh, accordingly, Flat No. A-82 was allotted to Trilochan Singh. After the allotment, Trilochan Singh sold the flat for Rs.19 lacs, out of this amount he received 3 lacs in cash and Rs.16 lacs by cheques. Accused Ajit Singh got a bank account in the name of Trilochan Singh opened in Punjab and Sind Bank, Paschim Vihar, New Delhi in which the said cheques were deposited. Then, accused Ajit Singh withdrew the said amount from the above account through various cheques. All such subsequent forgery, fabrication, manipulations of the record for allocation of individual flats to respective members is attributed to Ajit Singh in conspiracy with Ashwani Sharma, Naveen Kaushik as well as Ashutosh Pant.

31. No further act or involvement in the affairs of the Society is alleged against the accused/ respondent following the assuming of office by Ajit Singh as Secretary of the Society, he is not alleged to have participated in the fabrication of the record subsequent to the submission of the revised list of 90 members, fabricated documents accompanying his affidavit dated 27.02.1998. It is pertinent however that Ajit Singh who took possession of the land assigned and fabricated the record to induct members of his choice and get flats allotted to such selected members, himself was inducted in pursuance to fake proceedings and was shown to have been made Secretary also founded on fake election proceedings with the connivance and involvement, allegedly, of the accused /respondent.

32. Ajit Singh is got inducted when the allotment of land to the Page No. 28 of 35 Societies was being processed by RCS office and DDA authorities. Up until then the office bearers of the Society had made no effort to complete the verification process of the list of 90 members tendered earlier way back in the year 1985/1986. All of a sudden when the process for allotment of land to the societies registered with RCS was underway Ajit Singh is taken in, list is revised, members are shown as resigned, fresh members are enrolled and freeze strength of the Society is taken to 90. Both, the timing and the manner in which Ajit Singh is inducted and made the Secretary, for a prima facie case, at this stage is sufficient to proceed against the accused/respondent Avinash Chander for having conspired with Ajit Singh to get land allotted in favour of the Society and flats assigned to select members, of their choice, at concessional rates. This is what is alleged to be the larger conspiracy in the present case. Record was fabricated and prepared with such end in view to achieve this illegal purpose of allotment of land to the Society, and members are shown as resigned and enrolled to achieve the objective of allocation of flats to select members of choice.

33. It is the precise allegation of the prosecution that Ajit Singh, accused/respondent Avinash Chander (A-2), Ashwani Sharma (A-3), Naveen Kaushik (A-4) and Ashutosh Pant (A-5) entered into a criminal conspiracy during the year 1998 to 2004 and in furtherance of said criminal conspiracy resignations of some genuine members were forged and accepted and in their places new embers of their own choice were enrolled for allotment of land to the Society from DDA and thereafter Page No. 29 of 35 allotment of flats to the said members, causing wrongful loss to DDA and RCS by getting the land allotted at concessional rate and corresponding wrongful gain to themselves.

34. It is not necessary that every conspirator is privy to all the acts done nor that he partakes in all the acts committed in furtherance thereof, it is not even essential that he is aware of all and every acts done in pursuance thereto by every other of them, so long as he is shown to have shared in the common illegal object, and to have committed the act/ omission attributed towards the achievement of such illegal purpose. It is the unlawful agreement which is the gravamen of the crime of conspiracy. I shall not burden the present discussion with the manifold judgments on criminal conspiracy, but no discussion regarding the offence of criminal conspiracy is complete without reference to the broad principles culled by H'ble the Apex Court in State v. Nalini (1999) 5 SCC 253, summarised as follows:-

"583. Some of the broad principles governing the law of conspiracy may be summarised though, as the name implies, a summary cannot be exhaustive of the principles:
1. u/Sec. 120-A IPC offence of criminal conspiracy is committed when two or more persons agree to do or cause to be done an illegal act or legal act by illegal means. When it is a legal act by illegal means overt act is necessary. Offence of criminal conspiracy is an exception to the general law where intent alone does not constitute crime. It is intention to commit crime and joining hands with persons having the same intention. Not only the intention but there has to be agreement to carry out the object of the intention, which is an offence. The question for consideration in a case is did all the accused have the intention and did they agree that the crime be committed. It would not be enough for the offence of conspiracy when some of the accused merely entertained a wish, howsoever horrendous it may be, that offence be committed.
2. Acts subsequent to the achieving of the object of conspiracy may tend to prove that a particular accused was party to the Page No. 30 of 35 conspiracy. Once the object of conspiracy has been achieved, any subsequent act, which may be unlawful, would not make the accused a part of the conspiracy like giving shelter to an absconder.
3. Conspiracy is hatched in private or in secrecy. It is rarely possible to establish a conspiracy by direct evidence. Usually, both the existence of the conspiracy and its objects have to be inferred from the circumstances and the conduct of the accused.
4. Conspirators may for example, be enrolled in a chain -- A enrolling B, B enrolling C, and so on; and all will be members of a single conspiracy if they so intend and agree, even though each member knows only the person who enrolled him and the person whom he enrols. There may be a kind of umbrella-spoke enrolment, where a single person at the centre does the enrolling and all the other members are unknown to each other, though they know that there are to be other members. These are theories and in practice it may be difficult to tell which conspiracy in a particular case falls into which category. It may however, even overlap. But then there has to be present mutual interest. Persons may be members of single conspiracy even though each is ignorant of the identity of many others who may have diverse roles to play. It is not a part of the crime of conspiracy that all the conspirators need to agree to play the same or an active role.
5. When two or more persons agree to commit a crime of conspiracy, then regardless of making or considering any plans for its commission, and despite the fact that no step is taken by any such person to carry out their common purpose, a crime is committed by each and every one who joins in the agreement.

There has thus to be two conspirators and there may be more than that. To prove the charge of conspiracy it is not necessary that intended crime was committed or not. If committed it may further help prosecution to prove the charge of conspiracy.

6. It is not necessary that all conspirators should agree to the common purpose at the same time. They may join with other conspirators at any time before the consummation of the intended objective, and all are equally responsible. What part each conspirator is to play may not be known to everyone or the fact as to when a conspirator joined the conspiracy and when he left.

7. A charge of conspiracy may prejudice the accused because it forces them into a joint trial and the court may consider the entire mass of evidence against every accused. Prosecution has to produce evidence not only to show that each of the accused has knowledge of the object of conspiracy but also of the agreement. In the charge of conspiracy the court has to guard itself against the danger of unfairness to the accused. Introduction of evidence against some may result in the conviction of all, which is to be avoided. By means of evidence in conspiracy, which is otherwise Page No. 31 of 35 inadmissible in the trial of any other substantive offence prosecution tries to implicate the accused not only in the conspiracy itself but also in the substantive crime of the alleged conspirators. There is always difficulty in tracing the precise contribution of each member of the conspiracy but then there has to be cogent and convincing evidence against each one of the accused charged with the offence of conspiracy. As observed by Judge Learned Hand 'this distinction is important today when many prosecutors seek to sweep within the dragnet of conspiracy all those who have been associated in any degree whatever with the main offenders'.

8. As stated above it is the unlawful agreement and not its accomplishment, which is the gist or essence of the crime of conspiracy. Offence of criminal conspiracy is complete even though there is no agreement as to the means by which the purpose is to be accomplished. It is the unlawful agreement which is the gravamen of the crime of conspiracy. The unlawful agreement which amounts to a conspiracy need not be formal or express, but may be inherent in and inferred from the circumstances, especially declarations, acts and conduct of the conspirators. The agreement need not be entered into by all the parties to it at the same time, but may be reached by successive actions evidencing their joining of the conspiracy.

9. It has been said that a criminal conspiracy is a partnership in crime, and that there is in each conspiracy a joint or mutual agency for the prosecution of a common plan. Thus, if two or more persons enter into a conspiracy, any act done by any of them pursuant to the agreement is, in contemplation of law, the act of each of them and they are jointly responsible therefor. This means that everything said, written or done by any of the conspirators in execution or furtherance of the common purpose is deemed to have been said, done or written by each of them. And this joint responsibility extends not only to what is done by any of the conspirators pursuant to the original agreement but also to collateral acts incidental to and growing out of the original purpose. A conspirator is not responsible, however, for acts done by a co-conspirator after termination of the conspiracy. The joinder of a conspiracy by a new member does not create a new conspiracy nor does it change the status of the other conspirators, and the mere fact that conspirators individually or in groups perform different tasks to a common end does not split up a conspiracy into several different conspiracies.

10. A man may join a conspiracy by word or by deed. However, criminal responsibility for a conspiracy requires more than a merely passive attitude towards an existing conspiracy. One who commits an overt act with knowledge of the conspiracy is guilty. And one who tacitly consents to the object of a conspiracy and Page No. 32 of 35 goes along with other conspirators, actually standing by while the others put the conspiracy into effect, is guilty though he intends to take no active part in the crime."

35. Recapitulating, the revised list of 90 members submitted with the affidavit of the respondent dated 27.02.1998 controlled the freeze strength, land was allocated on the basis thereof, and flats were to be assigned in accordance therewith. It is brought on record that there were five such members who had not even applied for membership, all documents pertaining to them are alleged to have been forged, forged affidavits of four of the members of the Society were supplied, the resignations and refunds issued to five of its erstwhile members were not genuine, the proceedings of the Society were fabricated in consonance therewith, all as per the prosecution, in pursuance to and as part of a criminal conspiracy hatched with Ajit Singh who was inducted as a member and office bearer fraudulently, who then proceeded to take possession of the land assigned, and is attributed numerous acts and omissions in ensuring that flats get allocated to members as selected by him.

36. The accused/respondent by his such acts and omissions is shown prima facie to be part of this larger conspiracy to get allotted land in favour of the Society and the flats in the names of members chosen by the then Secretary to the Society, at concessional rates, even if Ashwani Sharma and Naveen Kaushik were roped in later, allegedly, by Ajit Singh and land was allotted and flats allocated after he had resigned from the membership of the Society. It is pertinent that though the respondent has contended that he had resigned from the membership in Page No. 33 of 35 December, 1997, he has himself admitted to have managed the affairs of the Society thereafter also and to have participated in the induction of Ajit Singh as a member and then as an office bearer, assuming all control of the affairs of the Society. It is immaterial that he himself was not allotted any flat, delivery of property to any person is required to be shown not necessarily to the accused alleged to have dishonestly induced the same, for the purposes of proceeding against the accused u/Sec. 420 IPC.

37. There is then sufficient basis for proceeding against the respondent/accused Avinash Chander for the offences u/Sec. 120- B r/w Sec. 420 IPC and the substantive offence u/Sec. 420 IPC. The Ld. Trial Court has erred in discharging the respondent/accused Avinash Chander for the offences u/Sec. 120- B r/w Sec. 420 IPC and the substantive offence u/Sec. 420 IPC without appreciating the entire facts and circumstances appearing on the record. The reliance on the judgment of H'ble the High Court of Delhi rendered in A. P. Narang Vs. CBI (Cr. R.P. No. 397/2010, DOD 17.01.2011) is also misplaced in such facts and circumstances as brought forth above, even otherwise the allegation here is not that the individual members had been deceived and deprived of any rights or interest, it is the RCS office and DDA that were induced by the accused into verifying a fabricated list of members and to have allotted land to the Society and plots to those enrolled as members at concessional rates, in connivance with one another.

38. As a consequence of the discussion above, the present revision petition succeeds on merits. Order dated 14.11.2019 Page No. 34 of 35 passed by Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap, the then Ld. CMM, Rouse Avenue Court, New Delhi, is set aside to the extent that respondent/accused Avinash Chander has been discharged of the offence u/Sec.120-B r/w Sec. 420 IPC and the substantive offence u/Sec. 420 IPC with the direction that charges be framed against him accordingly. Revision petition accordingly stands allowed.

39. Needless to say that the observations made above and the conclusions arrived shall have no bearing on the final outcome and are not to be construed as conclusive and binding on any aspect of the matter and are made strictly for the purposes of disposal of the present revision petition.

Trial Court record be returned with copy of this order. Revision file be consigned to Record Room.
